prompt: Create a high-fidelity flat desktop web UI design comp for World Wide Maze /admin. 1440x1000 landscape viewport, full bleed actual interface, no physical scene or browser chrome. Established visual identity fixed across all options: warm off-white #f7f6f2 background, near-white panels #fffefb, ink #16181d, muted #5d6370, fine #d8d4c9 separators, deep teal #0b6f79 primary action/selection, pale teal #dcefef. Instrument Sans-style contemporary humanist sans for ALL type, readable 14-16px body, compact 28px headings, 4px corners and normal form controls; no serif, gradients, glass, giant metrics, bento tiles, decorative graphics, shadow effects, avatars, or invented features. This is an operator tool for reviewing captured website screenshots and pausing services. Header says World Wide Maze / Administration; small "Design preview · illustrative data" disclaimer. Use real task vocabulary: Review captures, Capture attempts, Services & budget, URL & domain rules, Jev. Top compact status reads "Capture enabled · Manual review" and "September reserve $10.04 / $50 target". Reserved spend is not actual billing; do not claim overall health. Review queue contains Example Domain, Disney.com, Labyrinth — Wikipedia, Google News with Pending review labels and compact capture dates. Selected Example Domain inspector uses a simple retained screenshot showing heading Example Domain and the ordinary short documentation placeholder prose inside a pale webpage; label it "Capture evidence". Screenshot viewer toggle and visible text "1 slice". User actions "Approve run", "Block run", "Return to review"; approval button leads to a confirmation, not instant approval. Metadata below screenshot: "Captured Sep 25" "Artifacts retained" "Human review"; short reason textarea and collapsed "URL rules and history". Keep advanced deletion out of primary actions. All text, dividers and controls should be crisp, plausible, carefully aligned, professionally crafted, with generous but efficient whitespace. No fake charts or fabricated counts. COMPOSITION A — TABBED REVIEW WORKBENCH. Slim 64px global header and status strip. Under header a horizontal task navigation row with Review captures selected via teal underline. A compact heading "Review captures" and subtext "Inspect captured pages before making them available." with search URL and status filter on one line. The remaining viewport is a two-column workbench: narrow 32% queue left, expansive 68% evidence inspector right, separated by a thin vertical rule. Queue selected row pale teal. Inspector includes screenshot and decision controls clearly visible at once. Queue has Page 1 and Previous/Next at bottom. Make this calm, extremely comprehensible, task-focused. No sidebar.
notes: Illustrative layout, not new product claims. Correct generated dates and service descriptions. Review reasons remain required; no page-source viewer or sorting feature implied. Keep existing explicit confirmation.
